title: System Design Interview - An insiders guide volume 3

blocks.text: In this chapter, we talked about consistent hashing. This is a method used to manage how data is stored across servers. It's important because it helps to evenly distribute data. Here are the main points about consistent hashing.
When servers are added or removed, minimal keys need to be redistributed.
It allows for easy horizontal scaling because data is shared more evenly.

It helps solve the hotspot key problem, where too much traffic to a single storage area (shard) can overload a server. For example, if data for Katy Perry, Justin Bieber, and Lady Gaga is all on the same shard, it could cause issues. Consistent hashing spreads out this data.
Consistent hashing is used in many popular systems, such as:
Partitioning part of Amazon's Dynamo database.
Distributing data across the cluster in Apache Cassandra.
Handling data in Discord chat application.
Managing content delivery in Akamai network.
Congratulations on making it this far! Give yourself a pat on the back. Good job!

script:
We talked about consistent hashing. This method arranges how we store data across our servers. It spreads out the data efficiently, which is key.

When you add or remove servers, consistent hashing means only a few pieces of data need to change hands. This makes it easier to grow, or scale, the system horizontally. You can just add servers without worrying about huge shifts in data.

You see it in lots of systems. For instance, Amazon's Dynamo database uses it to partition data. Apache Cassandra relies on it for data distribution. Discord uses it to manage chat data. Even services like Akamai and Maglev count on consistent hashing to balance loads. It's a big part of modern architecture.
